transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Um, yeah… thanks. I guess it’s work stuff, mostly. I’m a barber, and I’ve been having a really hard time with the straight razor. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it’s gotten to where I’ll do pretty much anything to avoid using it—like switch clients, say I can’t find the blade, or just keep it hidden in the drawer.

And if I can’t get out of it, I kind of… shake through the whole shave. It’s embarrassing, honestly. I know that probably sounds ridiculous, but that’s why I came in.
Is it specifically the straight razor that causes you this anxiety, or do you also feel similar discomfort with other tools or situations at work?

It’s mainly the straight razor, yeah. I mean, I’m fine with clippers and scissors and the regular tools—I use those all day without thinking much about it.

But when the straight razor is open at my station… I know it’s just a tool, and I trained with it, but it feels like I’m suddenly about to hurt somebody or cut myself really badly. I know that probably sounds dramatic, but that’s the part that gets to me.
Have you ever felt this way about anything else—like a specific object or situation that makes you feel intense anxiety, even if you know it’s irrational?

Not really with anything else that I can think of. It’s… mostly that razor. I know it’s just a tool, and I mean, I trained with it—I use clippers all day and I’m fine. But when the straight razor is sitting there open at my station, it just feels like I’m about to hurt somebody or cut myself badly.

I know that probably sounds irrational. That’s kind of why I feel stupid saying it, but… yeah, that’s the thing that sets it off.
Outside of work, do you find yourself avoiding anything else—like certain places, activities, or objects—because it makes you feel anxious or fearful?

Outside of work, not really… I mean, nothing I can think of like that. It’s mostly just the straight razor at the shop.

I don’t want to make it sound like I’m completely falling apart, but I’ve gotten to where I’ll do almost anything to not use it—switch clients, say the blade’s missing, keep it hidden in the drawer. And if I really can’t avoid it, I’m… I’m shaking through the shave. It’s embarrassing to admit, honestly.
Have you ever had sudden episodes of intense fear or discomfort, like a panic attack, in situations other than when you’re around the straight razor?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had normal stress, like anyone, but not those sudden intense episodes out of nowhere.

It really seems tied to the straight razor. That’s when it happens. If I’m not around that, I’m usually okay… at least as far as I’ve noticed.
Does this fear of the straight razor cause you a lot of distress, or has it affected your ability to do your job or other parts of your life?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it has started causing problems at work.

I’ve lost some tips, and a couple regular clients have complained because I keep avoiding razor shaves or passing them off to the other barbers. And there was this barber battle I was supposed to do, but I backed out once I found out razor detailing was required.

So… yeah, I guess it’s affecting my job more than I’d like to admit.
How long have you felt this way about the straight razor? Has this fear been present for at least six months?

Yeah… it’s been more than six months. I’d say about 11 months now, roughly.

It kind of started around when I was having those arguments with the shop owner about the straight-razor shave package. I thought it would pass, honestly, so I didn’t really make a big deal of it at first… but it’s still there.
